thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate observed at api-edge/gateway cluster in us-east-1 — 502/504 spike (current 5xx ~4.6%, baseline 0.3%) — paging oncall.
pagerduty: Paging jamie (oncall) — please acknowledge.
jamie: ack'd. I'm on it. grabbing dashboards.
ravi: I see same in grafana — spike starts ~10:22 UTC and coincides with a spike in average upstream connection time. p50 latency up from 40ms to 220ms.
sasha: any recent deploys or config changes around 10:20-10:25?
jamie: quick check — no API gateway code deploys in that window. There was a WAF rule rollout at 10:15 by infra-team (change-id: waf-2026-08). pulling the waf rollout notes.
maria: also seeing increased 429s for a small subset of internal bots — might be cascading.
kevin: adding logs from the edge LB:
```
[2026-05-14T10:22:14Z] gw-edge-12 ERROR upstream timeout for backend redwood-api-v2 host=10.12.4.23:504
[2026-05-14T10:22:15Z] gw-edge-07 ERROR connection reset by peer
```
jamie: looks like upstreams are timing out rather than returning 502 bodies — could be overloaded backends or network flapping.
sasha: can someone query /metrics on the gateway and the backend pods? i want to see in-flight requests and queue lengths.
ravi: running:
```
curl -s http://grafana.internal/d/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query?query=sum(go_goroutines)%20by%20(job)
```
ravi: gateway goroutines jumped ~3x; backend app pods show increased p95 processing time.
jamie: start mitigation checklist: 1) reduce incoming concurrency at gateway, 2) enable fallback to read-only region for non-critical paths, 3) scale backend pool up, 4) consider rolling back waf rule if correlated.
maria: scaling backend pools now: increasing replicas on redwood-api-prod from 24 -> 36, applying HPA override.
kevin: I'm temporarily diverting non-critical traffic to our replica region via traffic-split policy (50% -> us-west-2). applying now.
product-ops: notifying top customers; need ETA on recovery and list of impacted endpoints.
jamie: quick customer impact summary: all text-generation endpoints experienced elevated errors; embeddings unaffected. A subset of long-running chat sessions had the worst impact. initial customer-facing ETA: 30-45m.
sasha: I'm running an edge debug to capture socket stats. command:
```
ss -ntp | grep 10.12
```
sasha: seeing many connections stuck in SYN-RECV to backend host 10.12.4.23 — suggests networking or backend process not accepting new conns.
ravi: checking pod health on that host: kubelet reports OOM kills on redwood-api-10.12.4.23 around 10:21.
jamie: that would explain timeouts. any recent model-load or memory spike jobs targeting that node?
kevin: there was a scheduled nightly model cache refresh but it runs at 03:00 UTC. nothing scheduled at 10:20.
maria: OOMs are weird — maybe memory leak triggered by increased concurrency. scaling should help buying time.
jamie: mitigation update: 1) scaled pods (in progress), 2) traffic split applied, 3) enabling short-term circuit breaker at gateway for requests > 90s, 4) WAF rule rollback candidate queued.
sasha: rolling back WAF rule (waf-2026-08) would take ~4m. if rollback stops extra processing on gateway, might help.
ravi: what's the risk of rollback? any security concern?
kevin: waf rule was a rate-based anomaly filter for API keys; safe to rollback short-term — we've reverted similar before.
jamie: go ahead with waf rollback if no objections.
product-ops: please add a line to the outgoing status message: "We have applied traffic-splitting and scaled capacity; investigating root cause related to backend process instability."
maria: waf rule rollback in flight — `infra-deploy rollback waf-2026-08` -> done. seeing slight drop in gateway CPU.
jamie: backend replicas are coming up; OOMs have stopped for the last 2 checks on affected nodes.
sasha: p95 latency trending down from 1.4s to 320ms — still above baseline but improving.
kevin: reverting traffic-split gradually to 80/20 (us-east/us-west) to validate stability.
ravi: error-rate dropped from 4.6% -> 0.8% after rollback + scaling. still not at baseline but much better.
jamie: ok, immediate mitigation successful. next steps: - keep extra replicas for 2 hours - run heap/profile on affected pod image to find leak - correlate with any client payload patterns - produce an incident report and customer notification.
product-ops: drafting status update to customers now. include affected endpoints, mitigation steps taken, and next ETA for RCA (48h).
incident-bot: NOTE: escalation timer -> if error-rate >1% for next 15m, auto-escalate to SevOps.
jamie: I'll keep watch for the next 30m and then hand off to second-shift oncall (ravi) at 11:00 UTC. leaving detailed checklist in thread.
jamie: checklist appended:
- [x] acked page
- [x] collected initial metrics (grafana, logs)
- [x] increased replicas
- [x] applied traffic split
- [x] rolled back waf rule
- [x] validated error-rate improving
- [ ] run heap/profile on affected images (assigned: sasha)
- [ ] full incident report (assigned: jamie)
- [ ] customer notification (assigned: product-ops)
ravi: taking watch at 11:00 UTC. leaving monitoring alerts set and a link to the runbook: https://wiki.internal/incidents/gateway-5xx-runbook
sasha: I'll collect heap dump and flame graphs; filing a bug with logs attached.
kevin: marking this incident as mitigated in ops-tooling; keeping the channel open for RCA.
product-ops: sent customer comms: "We mitigated the elevated error rates by scaling and rolling back an infra WAF rule; we're investigating root cause and will follow up within 48 hours." customers acked.
jamie: handing off now to ravi. good work all. :tada:
ravi: thanks — monitoring. will update if anything regresses.
incident-bot: Incident state changed -> MITIGATED (partial) at 11:05 UTC."
